harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built an Ansible-driven WireGuard gateway topology on the Antrieb cluster: node2 serves an application on TCP 8080 bound only to a private LAN interface shared with node1 (10.10.20.0/24, the environment's egress:false "lan" network); node1 (VyOS) terminates a WireGuard tunnel (wg0, 10.10.30.0/24) for node3 and NAT-masquerades tunnel traffic onto the LAN so node2 sees requests as coming from node1. node3, which sits only on the shared mgmt network, can reach node2:8080 exclusively through the tunnel — direct attempts return connection failure, tunneled attempts return HTTP 200. All configuration was applied via a single Ansible playbook run from the designated control_node (node4), using SSH auth wired up with the cluster's shared keypair. All four managed nodes were then restarted one at a time via their native reboot mechanisms; boot-id changes were captured as proof of each restart, and full functional recovery (WireGuard handshake, NAT-forwarded HTTP access, blocked direct access) was reverified after every restart.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 4 nodes' interfaces/routes and read environment.toml, discovering the mgmt network (10.100.198.0/24, dhcp+egress, all nodes) and the lan network (dhcp:false, egress:false, only node1 eth1 + node2 eth1)

Wired up passwordless SSH from control_node node4 to node1 (vyos user) and node2/node3 (root) using the cluster-shared CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY/PRIVKEY: fixed node1's vyos authorized_keys, unlocked Alpine's locked root accounts on node2/node3 and installed the shared pubkey

Wrote an Ansible inventory (gateway/appserver/client groups) and a 5-play playbook under ~/wireguard-gateway on node4: (1) generate WG keypair on node1, (2) bootstrap node3 (apk wireguard-tools/python3) and generate its keypair, (3) configure node1 as VyOS WireGuard server (wg0 10.10.30.1/24:51820) + source-NAT masquerade of the wg subnet onto eth1 + firewall allow rules, via the script-template/configure/commit/save pattern, (4) deploy a python3 http.server app on node2 bound to its private LAN IP (10.10.20.2:8080) as a persistent OpenRC service, with static eth1 addressing persisted in /etc/network/interfaces, (5) configure node3's wg-quick client (wg0 10.10.30.2/24) with AllowedIPs restricted to only node2's LAN address, enabled via OpenRC symlink
Ran ansible-playbook end-to-end successfully (verified idempotent on re-run)

Functionally verified: node3 -> node2:8080 direct (mgmt IP) fails; node3 -> node2:8080 via tunnel (LAN IP, routed over wg0) returns HTTP 200 with node2's access log showing the source as node1's LAN IP (NAT working); node4 direct access also fails

Captured boot_id + service-health baseline on all 4 nodes, then restarted node4, node2, node3, and node1 one at a time via native reboot, polling until exec access returned, confirming changed boot_id each time, and reverifying WireGuard handshake, app service, and end-to-end tunnel-only reachability after each restart

evidence.requirement: App served from node2 on TCP 8080
evidence.summary: Playbook deployed and started the OpenRC 'webapp' service (python3 http.server on 8080 bound to 10.10.20.2); rc-service status shows started and curl to it returns the app content

evidence.requirement: node3 reaches node2:8080 only via WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1, not directly
evidence.summary: From node3: direct curl to node2's mgmt IP:8080 returns HTTP 000 (unreachable) while curl to node2's LAN IP:8080 (routed via wg0 AllowedIPs) returns the app content; node2's own httpd log shows the request source as node1's LAN IP confirming NAT via the gateway; node4 (outside the tunnel) also fails direct access

evidence.requirement: Implemented using Ansible from the correct control_node
evidence.summary: ansible-playbook run from node4 (the environment-declared control_node) against inventory covering node1 (vyos), node2, and node3, completing all 5 plays with ok/changed and no failures

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 2674ee60 with wg0/eth1 healthy; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id b6e943ce (changed); eth0 dhcp/eth1 lan/wg0 all restored from saved VyOS config; node3-to-node2 tunnel access recovered (HTTP 200) with fresh handshake and node2 log confirming NAT-forwarded traffic

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 38428064 with webapp started and eth1 addressed; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 0a0f04a8 (changed); eth1 static IP, webapp service, and tunnel-routed HTTP access to the app all recovered automatically

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 7dc2462b with wg-quick.wg0 started and tunnel handshake active; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id d1d2f2fe (changed); wg-quick.wg0 auto-started, new handshake established, tunnel access to node2 returns HTTP 200, direct access to node2's mgmt IP still fails

evidence.requirement: node4 (control_node) restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 489b0bb4; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 6eea0103 (changed); ansible -m ping to all three managed nodes succeeded afterward, confirming the Ansible control plane and its SSH key material persisted and are functional
